data.description:
## Context / Problem

The security gate blocks every pull request on an established repository, because it scans the whole checkout rather than the change. `scan_change` in `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:76` passes `req.repo_root` straight into `ScanTarget`, and every finding anywhere in the tree is then allowed to set a scanner verdict to "block".

A pilot run against `archive-massgov-pfml` made the consequence concrete. A two line portal change produced 606 findings, 93 of them blocking, and none of them related to the change. They sat in pre-existing infrastructure such as `.github/actions/build-image/action.yml`. Promotion returned `allow:false` with `gate_failed:semgrep,trivy`.

Because `_open_pull_request` runs only after `POLICY_ALLOWED` in `services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py:643`, this is what currently stops the platform opening a pull request at all. Any client repository with an existing finding backlog is affected the same way.

## Approach

Attribute findings to the files the change actually touched, and let only those findings set a scanner verdict. Keep every finding in the evidence record.

This fits better than the scanner-specific alternative. Semgrep offers `--baseline-commit`, but trivy has no equivalent, so a per-scanner approach would fix one tool and leave the other blocking. Filtering on attributed paths sits above the adapters, so it works for both tools and for any scanner added later, which matches how the gate is meant to generalise across client stacks.

Separating "what we found" from "what may block" also preserves the audit trail. Downgrading the scan itself would lose the pre-existing findings entirely, and those are worth recording even when they are not this change's responsibility.

The behaviour is fail-safe. When the changed set cannot be determined, when `base_ref` is empty, or when a finding carries no location to attribute, the gate falls back to blocking exactly as it does now. A repository-wide audit stays available through a `scan_scope` setting.

## Scope

- `services/orchestration/gates/scan_scope.py` is new and holds `changed_paths` and `blocking_findings`.
- `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py` computes the changed set and uses it when deriving `scanner_verdicts`, leaving the evidence records untouched.
- `scripts/config.py` gains `scan_scope`, defaulting to `changed`, with `repository` restoring current behaviour.
- `docs/gate-engine.md` documents the setting and the fail-safe fallbacks.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_scan_scope.py` is new.

## Grounded assumptions

- `base_ref` already reaches the activity. `draft_pull_request.py:1832` passes `base_ref=params.base_sha`, and `ScanChangeRequest.base_ref` is declared at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/security.py:22`. No new plumbing is needed.
- No adapter reads `base_ref` today. `RealSemgrepScanner.scan` at `adapters/real/security_scanner.py:142` builds its argument list from `target.repo_root` alone, which is why the scan is repository-wide.
- The changed set is computable where the activity runs. `git diff --name-only <base>..<ref>` executed in the workspace on the activity worker returns the two changed files for the pilot execution, against git 2.47.3.
- Finding locations are a path followed by a colon suffix. Semgrep emits `path:line` at `adapters/real/security_scanner.py:86` and trivy emits `target:package@version` at line 120, so a finding is attributed to a changed path when its location equals that path or begins with that path and a colon. No format-specific parsing is required.
- Locations are repository-relative by the time the gate sees them, because `restore_paths` in `services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py` rewrites pod paths before the findings are returned.

## Testing

Happy path: a change touching one file, with blocking findings in that file and in an untouched file, yields a verdict of "block" and records both findings as evidence.

Failure and edge paths: a change whose findings all sit in untouched files yields "pass" while still recording every finding. An empty `base_ref` falls back to repository scope and blocks. A `git` invocation that fails falls back to repository scope and blocks. A finding with an empty location blocks. `scan_scope` set to `repository` reproduces current behaviour. A location sharing a prefix with a changed path, such as `portal/src/pages/save-profile.tsx.bak` against `portal/src/pages/save-profile.tsx`, is not attributed to it.

Live end to end: re-running the pilot ticket against `archive-massgov-pfml` reaches `POLICY_ALLOWED` and opens a pull request.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A blocking finding in an unchanged file does not set a scanner verdict, verified by `tests/unit/test_scan_scope.py`.
- [ ] A blocking finding in a changed file does set the verdict to "block", verified by the same test module.
- [ ] Every finding is still persisted as evidence regardless of attribution, verified by a unit test asserting the evidence record count is unchanged when scoping removes findings.
- [ ] An empty `base_ref`, a failing `git` call, and a finding with no location each fall back to blocking, verified by three unit tests.
- [ ] Prefix collisions do not falsely attribute a finding, verified by a unit test using a path and that path with a suffix appended.
- [ ] A live run of the pilot ticket reaches `POLICY_ALLOWED` and the workflow opens a pull request against `archive-massgov-pfml`.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
data.title: ADEVX-101: Scope security gate blocking verdicts to the files the change touched
